Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent [
 Order
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is final heard.

2 This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 15.11.2018, passed in MACC No.334/2016,
by the Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Barwani, whereby a total sum of Rs.2,47,000/- has been awarded to him by way of compensation.
3. As per the appellant, on 02.08.2016, at about 08:15 am, he alongwith Prakash was travelling on his motorcycle.

When they reached Bavangaja, respondent No.1, drove vehicle a bus bearing registration No.MP- 46-P/0343 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle, as a result of which, they fell down and appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9637 2 MA-611-2019 Motilal suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment where he remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.
4. The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for award of a sum of Rs.10 Lakhs to him by way of compensation.
The application was contested by non-applicants by filing their written statements to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, the claims tribunal has awarded Motilal @ Motisingh vs Kashiram on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159727880/
1 compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.
5. This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that his income which has been assessed as Rs.5000/- per month is very low.
He has proved that he was working as skilled labourer and was having sufficient income hence the same ought to have been assessed appropriately.
It is also submitted that in the accident, the appellant had suffered permanent disability to the extent of 33.41% but the claims Tribunal has illegally assessed the same at 10% only.
It is also submitted that the future prospects of rise in income have not at all been taken into consideration hence, it is submitted that the amount of compensation be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted, in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9637 3 MA-611-2019 8.
In his statement before the Court, the appellant had specifically stated that at the time of the accident, he was working as a skilled labourer.
In view of his work, it could not have been expected from him to have produced any documentary proof in support of the same.
There was no reason to disbelieve the statement of the appellant.

If the appellant had failed to prove his income then also he ought to have been considered at least to be a semi skilled labourer, in view of which his income deserves to be assessed at Rs. 6,850/- per month.
9. The Doctor who had issued the permanent disability certificate of the appellant had stated the permanent disability to be 33.41%.
In the accident, the appellant had suffered grievous injury on his right leg below the right limb which has affected the overall function of his body.

Even though, the fracture may have eventually healed, the disability suffered by the appellant would be permanent and it has not been shown that there is a possibility of the same improving in the future.
In my opinion, the permanent disability ought to have been assessed at 10%.

In view of the decisions of the Apex court from time to time, the future prospects of rise in income of appellant were mandatorily required to be taken into consideration but have not been so taken by the claims Tribunal.
10. The amount, which the appellant would be entitled for on amount of personal disability would be Rs. 6,850/- per month +25% for future prospects of rise in income.
The same would be multiplied by 12 for making it anually.
The multiplier of 15 applied by the claims Tribunal is correct.
Taking the permanent disability at 10%, the amount under this head comes to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9637 4 MA-611-2019 Rs. 1,54,125/-.
The amount awarded by claims Tribunal to the appellant under the other heads is correct.

Motilal @ Motisingh vs Kashiram on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159727880/
2 11.
The appellant is entitled for award of a total sum of Rs. 3,11,125/- to him by way of compensation whereas the claims Tribunal has erred in awarding him a sum of Rs. 2,47,000/- Only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement of award of compensation by Rs. 64,125 which would be paid to him along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
12. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE VD Motilal @ Motisingh vs Kashiram on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159727880/
